relationship: related setting apart of a measured holy land portion
rationale: Both passages set apart a first portion for the Lord with a length of twenty-five thousand. The supplied breadth is twenty thousand here, whereas 48:9 gives twenty-five thousand before describing the priests' portion; the different extents are preserved rather than silently equated.
source_text: “When you measure out the land as an inheritance, you will set apart a first portion for the Lord, a holy part of the land, twenty-five thousand long and twenty thousand broad. It will be holy throughout all its boundaries all around.

target_units.text: The first portion they set apart for the Lord will be twenty-five thousand long and twenty-five thousand broad.

From these will be the first portion of the holy areas for the priests: twenty-five thousand toward the north, a breadth of ten thousand toward the sea, a breadth of ten thousand toward the east, and a length of twenty-five thousand toward the south. The mountain of the holy places will be in its midst,

relationship: related five-hundred-square sanctuary boundary
rationale: The sanctuary receives a square of five hundred by five hundred, with a fifty-cubit interval around it. The earlier house measurement likewise describes a five-hundred enclosure distinguishing holy areas from the forewall; it does not repeat the fifty-cubit interval.
source_text: From this, a square of five hundred by five hundred will be for a sanctuary, with an interval of fifty cubits all around it.

target_units.text: The measurement of the house inside was completed. He brought me out by the gate facing east and measured the plan of the house all around in its arrangement.
He stood behind the gate facing east and measured five hundred with the measuring reed.
He turned toward the north and measured the north-facing side: five hundred cubits with the measuring reed.
He turned toward the sea and measured the sea-facing side: five hundred with the measuring reed.
He turned toward the south and measured opposite the south: five hundred with the measuring reed.

The four sides were measured with the same reed. He laid it out, with their enclosure all around: five hundred toward the east and five hundred cubits in breadth, to distinguish between the holy areas and the forewall in the arrangement of the house.

relationship: repeated sacred plot dimensions and sanctuary placement
rationale: A twenty-five-thousand by ten-thousand plot contains the sanctuary. The priests' holy portion in 48:10 has those same stated dimensions and the mountain of the holy places in its midst, giving a counterpart for the designated sacred plot rather than merely another measured area.
source_text: From this measured area you will measure a length of twenty-five thousand and a breadth of ten thousand. In it will be the sanctuary, the most holy place.

target_units.text: From these will be the first portion of the holy areas for the priests: twenty-five thousand toward the north, a breadth of ten thousand toward the sea, a breadth of ten thousand toward the east, and a length of twenty-five thousand toward the south. The mountain of the holy places will be in its midst,

relationship: repeated allocation of holy land to ministering priests
rationale: Land is assigned to the priests who draw near to minister to the Lord, including a place for their houses. The later allocation likewise sets apart a holy portion for priests and identifies the faithful sons of Zadok; that passage adds their identity and fidelity without repeating the housing clause.
source_text: It will be land for the priests who minister in the holy place, for those who draw near to minister to the Lord. It will be a place for their houses, set apart for their sanctification.

target_units.text: From these will be the first portion of the holy areas for the priests: twenty-five thousand toward the north, a breadth of ten thousand toward the sea, a breadth of ten thousand toward the east, and a length of twenty-five thousand toward the south. The mountain of the holy places will be in its midst,
for the consecrated priests, the sons of Zadok, who keep the duties of the house and did not stray when the sons of Israel strayed, as the Levites strayed.
They will have the first portion given from the land’s first portions, most holy, from the Levites’ boundaries.

relationship: parallel provision of dwelling places for Levites
rationale: The Levites who minister to the house receive land with cities in which to dwell. Numbers likewise requires Israel to give the Levites towns for dwelling and adjoining land, without supplying Ezekiel's twenty-five-thousand by ten-thousand allotment.
source_text: An area twenty-five thousand long and ten thousand broad will belong to the Levites who minister to the house, as their possession, with cities in which to dwell.

target_units.text: Instruct the sons of Israel to give the Levites towns to live in from their allotted possessions. They shall also give the Levites the outlying lands around the towns.
And the towns shall be theirs to live in, and their designated lands shall be for their livestock and all their four-footed animals.

relationship: repeated five-thousand-wide provision for the city
rationale: The city receives a possession five thousand broad and twenty-five thousand long. The later plan again reserves five thousand alongside twenty-five thousand for the city, dwelling and intervening space, there calling it a forewall and placing the city in its midst.
source_text: You will give the city a possession five thousand broad and twenty-five thousand long; like the first portion of the holy areas, these will be for the whole house of Israel.

target_units.text: The five thousand remaining in breadth alongside the twenty-five thousand will be a forewall for the city, for dwelling and its intervening space. The city will be in its midst.

relationship: repeated ruler's land beside holy and civic portions
rationale: The ruler receives land on either side of the holy first portions and the city's possession, extending toward the sea and east. The later allocation repeats those neighboring portions and directions, adding the twenty-five-thousand extent and the sanctuary in the midst.
source_text: The ruler will have land on this side and that side of the first portions of the holy areas and the city’s possession, facing the first portions of the holy areas and facing the city’s possession: the parts toward the sea, and from those toward the sea toward the east. Its length will be like one of the portions, from the sea-facing boundaries, with the length extending to the eastern boundaries of the land.

target_units.text: The remainder will belong to the ruler on this side and that side, from the holy first portions and toward the city’s possession, extending twenty-five thousand in length to the eastern boundaries, and toward the sea extending twenty-five thousand to the sea-facing boundaries, adjoining the ruler’s portions. The first portion of the holy areas and the house’s sanctuary will be in its midst.

relationship: related protection of Israel's inherited land from rulers' oppression
rationale: The ruler's possession is followed by a promise that Israel's rulers will no longer oppress the people and that the tribes will inherit land. Ezekiel 46 specifies that a ruler must give his sons land from his own possession rather than take the people's inheritance and scatter them from it.
source_text: It will be his possession in Israel. Israel’s rulers will no longer oppress My people, and the house of Israel will inherit the land according to their tribes.

target_units.text: The ruler will certainly not take from the people’s inheritance to oppress them. He will give his sons an inheritance from his own possession, so that none of My people is scattered from his possession.”

relationship: parallel royal duty to practice justice and remove oppression
rationale: Israel's rulers must remove injustice, suffering and oppression and practice judgment and righteousness. Jeremiah likewise addresses Judah's king with the duty to do justice and righteousness, rescue the wronged and refrain from oppression, naming particular vulnerable people.
source_text: Thus says the Lord God: Enough, rulers of Israel! Remove injustice and suffering, and practice judgment and righteousness. Take oppression away from My people, says the Lord God.

target_units.text: Thus says the Lord: Go and descend to the house of Judah’s king and speak this word there,
and say: Hear the Lord’s word, king of Judah who sits on David’s throne—you, your household, your people, and those entering these gates.

Thus says the Lord: Do justice and righteousness; rescue the plundered from the hand of the one wronging him. Do not oppress the newcomer, orphan, or widow, and do not act impiously or shed innocent blood in this place.

relationship: parallel requirement for honest weights and measures
rationale: Ezekiel requires an honest balance, measure and choenix. Leviticus likewise forbids injustice in measures, weights and scales and requires just scales, weights and a chous; the shared ethical standard does not identify the differently named capacity units.
source_text: You are to have an honest balance, an honest measure, and an honest choenix.

target_units.text: You shall do no injustice in judgment, in measures, weights, or scales.
You shall have just scales, just weights, and a just chous. I am the Lord your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt.

relationship: related consistency of capacity standards
rationale: Ezekiel makes the measure and choenix equal, each a tenth of the gomor. Deuteronomy forbids differing large and small household measures and requires a true, just measure; it supports consistent measurement without supplying Ezekiel's units or conversion.
source_text: The measure and the choenix will likewise have one capacity: the choenix a tenth of the gomor, and the measure a tenth of the gomor. They will be equal in relation to the gomor.

target_units.text: You shall not have in your house differing measures, a great and a small.
You shall have a true and just weight, and you shall have a true and just measure, that your days may be long upon the land which the Lord your God gives you for a possession.

relationship: shared twenty-obol weight standard
rationale: Ezekiel states that the standard weight is twenty obols before discussing shekels and a fifty-shekel mina. Numbers likewise defines the holy shekel as twenty obols in its redemption valuation, without supplying Ezekiel's mina calculation.
source_text: The standard weight will be twenty obols. The five shekels will be five, the ten shekels ten, and fifty shekels will make your mina.

target_units.text: And its redemption shall be from one month old; the valuation is five shekels by the holy shekel, which is twenty obols.

relationship: related grain contributions set apart for the Lord
rationale: Ezekiel specifies first portions from wheat and barley with named fractions and measures. Numbers likewise assigns grain firstfruits and the land's first produce given to the Lord to Aaron, but does not repeat the wheat-and-barley fractions or Ezekiel's later direction to the ruler.
source_text: This is the first portion you will set apart: a sixth of the measure from the gomor of wheat, and a sixth of the oiphi from the kor of barley.

target_units.text: Every firstfruit of oil, and every firstfruit of wine and grain, their firstfruits which they give unto the Lord, I have given them unto you.
All the first produce in their land, which they bring unto the Lord, shall be yours; everyone clean in your house shall eat it.

relationship: related sacred contribution of oil
rationale: The oil command assigns a cotyle from ten cotyles. Numbers likewise includes oil among firstfruits given to the Lord and assigned to Aaron; the counterpart concerns oil as a sacred contribution, not an identical fraction or recipient.
source_text: The command for oil is a cotyle of oil from ten cotyles, because ten cotyles are a gomor.

target_units.text: Every firstfruit of oil, and every firstfruit of wine and grain, their firstfruits which they give unto the Lord, I have given them unto you.

relationship: shared one-in-ten contribution from sheep
rationale: The supplied Ezekiel text takes one sheep from every ten as a contribution for sacrificial atonement. Leviticus likewise sets apart the tenth counted animal from cattle and sheep as holy to the Lord; it does not repeat Ezekiel's list of sacrificial purposes.
source_text: One sheep from every ten sheep will be a contribution from all Israel’s families, for sacrifices, burnt offerings, and offerings for well-being, to make atonement for you, says the Lord God.

target_units.text: And every tithe of cattle and sheep, and everything that comes under the staff in the count—the tenth shall be holy unto the Lord.

relationship: contrasting assigned recipients of Israel's sacred contributions
rationale: All the people give this first portion to Israel's ruler. Numbers instead gives Aaron charge of the firstfruits and assigns his family a share of Israel's holy contributions, distinguishing the recipients rather than identifying Ezekiel's ruler as the Aaronic priest.
source_text: All the people will give this first portion to Israel’s ruler.

target_units.text: And the Lord spoke unto Aaron: And I, behold, have given you charge of the firstfruits; from all things sanctified unto Me by the sons of Israel, I have given them unto you for a share of honour, and unto your sons after you, an everlasting ordinance.

And this shall be yours from the consecrated holy offerings: from all their gifts, and from all their sacrifices, and from every guilt offering of theirs, and from all their sin offerings which they render unto Me; from all the holy things it shall be yours and your sons’.
You shall eat them in the most holy place; every male shall eat them, you and your sons; they shall be holy unto you.

And this shall be yours, the firstfruits of their gifts: from all the presentations of the sons of Israel, I have given them unto you, and unto your sons and unto your daughters with you, an everlasting ordinance. Everyone clean in your house shall eat them.

relationship: parallel royal provision for Sabbath, new-moon and festival offerings
rationale: The ruler provides offerings for the house of Israel at Sabbaths, new moons and festivals. Chronicles likewise assigns the king's portion from his belongings to burnt offerings on those occasions, while additionally naming the morning and evening offerings.
source_text: Through the ruler will come the burnt offerings, sacrifices, and libations at the festivals, new moons, and Sabbaths, and at all the festivals of the house of Israel. He will provide the offerings for sin, the sacrifice, the burnt offerings, and the offerings for well-being to make atonement for the house of Israel.

target_units.text: Hezekiah arranged the divisions of priests and Levites, and each one’s divisions according to his own ministry, priests and Levites for the burnt offering and the sacrifice of salvation, to praise, give thanks, and minister at the gates in the courtyards of the Lord’s house.
The king’s portion from his belongings was for the morning and evening burnt offerings and burnt offerings for Sabbaths, new moons, and the festivals written in the Lord’s law.

relationship: related animal offerings for atonement of the holy place
rationale: Ezekiel prescribes an unblemished calf to make atonement for the holy place on the first day of the first month. Leviticus likewise makes atonement for the holy place through its calf-and-goat blood ritual, but does not give Ezekiel's date or identical ritual details.
source_text: Thus says the Lord God: In the first month, on the first of the month, you all will take an unblemished calf from the cattle to make atonement for the holy place.

target_units.text: And he shall take some of the calf’s blood and sprinkle it with his finger on the propitiatory cover toward the east; before the propitiatory cover he shall sprinkle some of the blood with his finger seven times.

And he shall slaughter the male young goat for the people’s sin offering before the Lord and bring some of its blood within the veil. He shall do with its blood as he did with the calf’s blood, sprinkling its blood on the propitiatory cover, before the propitiatory cover,

and make atonement for the holy place from the sons of Israel’s uncleannesses and their wrongdoings, concerning all their sins. He shall do the same for the Tent of Testimony established among them amid their uncleanness.

relationship: related application of atoning blood to sacred structures
rationale: Blood is placed on the house's doorposts, four corners of the sacred precinct, the altar and inner-court gateposts. The earlier altar rite likewise applies blood to four horns, four corners and the surrounding base; the particular locations differ and are not collapsed into one list.
source_text: The priest will take some of the blood of the atonement offering and put it on the house’s doorposts, on the four corners of the sacred precinct, on the altar, and on the doorposts of the gate of the inner court.

target_units.text: They will take some of its blood and put it on the altar’s four horns, on the four corners of the place of atonement, and on the base all around. They will make atonement for it.

relationship: contrasting seventh-month dates for sanctuary atonement
rationale: Ezekiel repeats atonement for the house on the first day of the seventh month. Leviticus places its observance on the tenth day and specifies atonement for the Holy of Holies, tent, altar, priests and congregation, preserving the shared month and purpose alongside the different day.
source_text: You will do likewise in the seventh month, on the first of the month: you will take a portion from each, and you all will make atonement for the house.

target_units.text: And this shall be an everlasting statute unto you: in the seventh month, on the tenth day of the month, humble your souls, and you shall do no work, neither the native nor the resident foreigner who is attached unto you.
For on this day he shall make atonement for you, to cleanse you from all your sins before the Lord; and you shall be cleansed.
It shall be a Sabbath of Sabbaths, a rest unto you; and you shall humble your souls: an everlasting statute.
The priest whom they anoint and whose hands they consecrate to serve as priest after his father shall make atonement. He shall put on the linen robe, a holy robe,
and he shall make atonement for the Holy of Holies, and for the Tent of Testimony and the altar shall he make atonement; and for the priests and for the whole congregation shall he make atonement.

relationship: shared Passover date and seven days of unleavened bread
rationale: Both passages place Passover on the fourteenth day of the first month and prescribe seven days of unleavened bread. Numbers separately names the fifteenth as the festival day, a distinction not stated separately in this Ezekiel unit.
source_text: In the first month, on the fourteenth of the month, you will have the Passover festival; for seven days you will eat unleavened bread.

target_units.text: And in the first month, on the fourteenth day of the month, is the Lord's Passover.
And on the fifteenth day of this month is a festival. You shall eat unleavened bread for seven days.

relationship: related sin offerings for the representative and the people
rationale: The ruler provides a calf for sin on behalf of himself, the house and all the people. Hebrews likewise describes a high priest offering for his own sins as well as the people's, comparing that representative pattern without identifying the ruler and priestly offices.
source_text: On that day the ruler will provide a calf for sin on behalf of himself, the house, and all the people of the land.

target_units.text: For every high priest taken from among people is appointed on behalf of people in matters concerning God, to offer both gifts and sacrifices for sins.
He can deal gently with those who are ignorant and wandering, since he too is surrounded by weakness,
and because of it he is obliged to make offerings for sins on his own behalf, just as on behalf of the people.

relationship: parallel seven-day festival sacrifices with different animal counts
rationale: Ezekiel requires seven calves, seven rams and a goat kid daily during the seven-day festival. Numbers likewise orders daily offerings for seven days, including a sin-offering goat, but names two calves, one ram and seven lambs rather than Ezekiel's cattle and ram counts.
source_text: For the seven days of the festival, he will provide burnt offerings to the Lord: seven calves and seven unblemished rams each day for the seven days, and a goat kid each day for sin.

target_units.text: And you shall bring whole burnt offerings, offerings unto the Lord: two calves from the cattle, one ram, seven year-old lambs; they shall be unblemished for you.
And their sacrifice shall be fine flour mixed with oil: three tenths for each calf and two tenths for each ram.
You shall prepare a tenth for each lamb, for the seven lambs;
And offer one male goat for sin, to make atonement for you,
besides the continual morning whole burning, which is a continual whole burnt offering.
These you shall prepare in this manner each day for seven days, a gift, an offering of sweet savour unto the Lord; besides the continual whole burnt offering you shall prepare its drink offering.

relationship: repeated cake-and-oil provision for calves and rams
rationale: Each calf and ram receives a cake, with a hin of oil for each cake. Ezekiel 46 repeats that provision and additionally leaves the lambs' offering to what the ruler's hand can produce, preserving the shared animal-specific provision and the added clause.
source_text: You will provide an offering of a cake for each calf and a cake for each ram, with a hin of oil for each cake.

target_units.text: A cake for the ram and a cake for the calf will be the grain offering, and for the lambs whatever his hand can produce, with a hin of oil for each cake.

relationship: shared seventh-month festival date and seven-day observance
rationale: Ezekiel places the festival on the fifteenth day of the seventh month and prescribes the offerings for seven days. Leviticus gives that same date and duration for the Feast of Tents, while also adding an eighth-day assembly that this Ezekiel unit does not state.
source_text: In the seventh month, on the fifteenth of the month, at the festival you will provide the same for seven days: the offerings for sin, the burnt offerings, the grain offering, and the oil.”

target_units.text: Speak to the sons of Israel, saying: On the fifteenth day of this seventh month is the Feast of Tents unto the Lord for seven days.
And on the first day there shall be a holy convocation. You shall do no laborious work.

For seven days you shall bring whole burnt offerings unto the Lord. The eighth day shall be a holy convocation for you, and you shall bring whole burnt offerings unto the Lord. It is a closing observance; you shall do no laborious work.

relationship: contrasting Sabbath gate arrangements for sanctuary and city
rationale: The sanctuary's eastern inner-court gate opens on the Sabbath, unlike its six working days. Nehemiah closes Jerusalem's gates until after the Sabbath to prevent burdens entering; the opposed gate arrangements serve different sanctuary and civic settings, not identical access rules.
source_text: “Thus says the Lord God: The gate in the inner court facing east will be shut during the six working days, but on the Sabbath day it will be opened, and on the day of the new moon it will be opened.

target_units.text: When the gates of Jerusalem were at rest before the Sabbath, I gave orders and they closed the gates. I ordered that they should not be opened until after the Sabbath. I stationed some of my young servants at the gates so that no burdens would be carried on the Sabbath day.
They all lodged and conducted sales outside Jerusalem once or twice.
I testified against them and said, “Why are you lodging opposite the wall? If you do it a second time, I will stretch out my hand against you.” From that time they did not come on the Sabbath.
I told the Levites who were purifying themselves and coming to guard the gates to sanctify the Sabbath day. In these things remember me, O God, and spare me according to the abundance of Thy mercy.

relationship: same-chapter shared place of worship for ruler and people
rationale: The ruler bows at the gate's vestibule, and the priests offer his sacrifices. The next unit places the people's bowing before the Lord at that gate's vestibules on Sabbaths and new moons, sharing the stated worship location without giving both groups identical entry privileges.
source_text: The ruler will enter by the porch of the outer gate and stand at the gate’s vestibules. The priests will offer his burnt offerings and his offerings for well-being. He will bow down at the gate’s vestibule and go out, and the gate will certainly not be shut until evening.

target_units.text: The people of the land will bow down before the Lord at the vestibules of that gate on Sabbaths and new moons.

relationship: parallel recurring monthly and Sabbath worship
rationale: The people bow before the Lord at the gate on Sabbaths and new moons. Isaiah likewise describes all flesh bowing before God in Jerusalem month after month and Sabbath after Sabbath; its supplied wording gives the recurring monthly rhythm rather than explicitly saying new moon.
source_text: The people of the land will bow down before the Lord at the vestibules of that gate on Sabbaths and new moons.

target_units.text: Month after month and Sabbath after Sabbath, all flesh will come before Me to bow down in Jerusalem,’ said the Lord.

relationship: parallel Sabbath lamb offerings with differing requirements
rationale: Ezekiel's Sabbath offering includes six unblemished lambs and an unblemished ram. Numbers likewise prescribes unblemished lambs for the Sabbath, but two year-old lambs with flour, oil and a drink offering, keeping the differing counts and additional details distinct.
source_text: The ruler will present burnt offerings to the Lord: on the Sabbath day, six unblemished lambs and an unblemished ram,

target_units.text: And on the Sabbath day you shall bring two unblemished year-old lambs, and two tenths of fine flour mixed with oil for a sacrifice, and a drink offering,
a Sabbath whole burnt offering on each Sabbath, besides the continual whole burning and its drink offering.

relationship: same-chapter repeated ram and lamb grain-offering provisions
rationale: The ram receives a cake, the lambs an offering as the gift of the ruler's hand, and each cake a hin of oil. Verse 7 repeats the ram's cake, the hand-dependent lamb offering and oil rate, while additionally specifying a cake for the calf.
source_text: with a grain offering of a cake for the ram, and for the lambs an offering as the gift of his hand, with a hin of oil for each cake.

target_units.text: A cake for the ram and a cake for the calf will be the grain offering, and for the lambs whatever his hand can produce, with a hin of oil for each cake.

relationship: parallel new-moon provision of calves, a ram and lambs
rationale: Ezekiel's new-moon offering names one calf, six lambs and a ram. Numbers likewise names cattle, a ram and lambs at new moons, but specifies two calves and seven lambs; the common occasion and animal types do not erase the numerical differences.
source_text: On the day of the new moon there will be an unblemished calf and six lambs, and the ram will be unblemished.

target_units.text: And at the new moons you shall bring whole burnt offerings unto the Lord: two calves from the cattle, and one ram, and seven unblemished year-old lambs;

relationship: same-chapter repeated grain-and-oil schedule at different observances
rationale: The calf and ram each receive a cake, the lamb offering depends on what the ruler's hand can produce, and each cake receives a hin of oil. Verse 11 repeats those provisions for festivals and public assemblies, extending the same stated schedule beyond the preceding new-moon setting.
source_text: A cake for the ram and a cake for the calf will be the grain offering, and for the lambs whatever his hand can produce, with a hin of oil for each cake.

target_units.text: At the festivals and public assemblies the grain offering will be a cake for each calf, a cake for each ram, and for the lambs whatever his hand can produce, with a hin of oil for each cake.

relationship: related ruler's entry through a gate porch and departure
rationale: The ruler enters through the gate's porch and goes out by the gate's way. Ezekiel 44 likewise gives the ruler a porch approach and departure by his way, there in the outer-gate setting and with eating bread before the Lord; the gates and additional actions are not silently equated.
source_text: When the ruler enters, he will enter by the porch of the gate and go out by the way of the gate.

target_units.text: for the ruler—he will sit in it to eat bread before the Lord. He will enter by the way of the gate’s porch and go out by his way.”

relationship: same-chapter distinction between stated routes for ruler and festival worshippers
rationale: Festival worshippers must leave by the gate opposite their entrance, north to south or south to north, and may not return through their entrance gate. Verse 8 instead describes the ruler's porch approach and departure by the gate's way, without repeating that explicit opposite-gate instruction.
source_text: When the people of the land come before the Lord at the festivals, whoever enters by the north gate to bow down will go out by the south gate, and whoever enters by the south gate will go out by the north gate. He will not return through the gate by which he entered, but will go out straight opposite it.

target_units.text: When the ruler enters, he will enter by the porch of the gate and go out by the way of the gate.

relationship: repeated calf-and-ram grain offering with a hin of oil
rationale: The festival and assembly schedule gives a cake for each calf and ram and a hin of oil for each cake. Ezekiel 45 gives that same calf-and-ram provision; the hand-dependent offering for lambs appears additionally in this unit.
source_text: At the festivals and public assemblies the grain offering will be a cake for each calf, a cake for each ram, and for the lambs whatever his hand can produce, with a hin of oil for each cake.

target_units.text: You will provide an offering of a cake for each calf and a cake for each ram, with a hin of oil for each cake.

relationship: same-chapter comparison of gate schedules and Sabbath practice
rationale: The pledged offering uses an east-facing gate, expressly compares the offering with Sabbath practice, and closes the doors after departure. Verses 1–2 give Sabbath and new-moon opening and an until-evening closure rule while mentioning an inner-court gate and an outer-gate porch; these schedules are compared without resolving the gate identities.
source_text: If the ruler makes a pledged offering, a burnt offering for well-being to the Lord, he will open for himself the gate facing east and offer his burnt offering and his offerings for well-being as he does on the Sabbath day. He will go out and close the doors after he has gone out.

target_units.text: “Thus says the Lord God: The gate in the inner court facing east will be shut during the six working days, but on the Sabbath day it will be opened, and on the day of the new moon it will be opened.

The ruler will enter by the porch of the outer gate and stand at the gate’s vestibules. The priests will offer his burnt offerings and his offerings for well-being. He will bow down at the gate’s vestibule and go out, and the gate will certainly not be shut until evening.

relationship: parallel daily unblemished year-old lamb offering in the morning
rationale: Ezekiel prescribes an unblemished year-old lamb as a daily burnt offering in the morning. Numbers likewise requires unblemished year-old lambs and assigns one to the morning, while also requiring a second toward evening, which this unit does not state.
source_text: He will prepare an unblemished year-old lamb as a daily burnt offering to the Lord; in the morning he will prepare it.

target_units.text: And you shall say unto them: These are the offerings which you shall bring unto the Lord: two unblemished year-old lambs each day for a continual whole burning;
you shall offer the one lamb in the morning, and you shall offer the second lamb toward evening.

relationship: parallel flour-and-oil offering with different stated ratios
rationale: Ezekiel gives a sixth of the measure and a third of a hin of oil to mix the fine flour. Numbers likewise mixes fine flour with oil for the daily offering, but states a tenth of an oiphi and a fourth of a hin; the units and fractions are preserved without forced conversion.
source_text: In the morning he will prepare with it a grain offering of a sixth of the measure and a third of a hin of oil to mix the fine flour: a grain offering to the Lord, a permanent command.

target_units.text: And you shall prepare a tenth of an oiphi of fine flour for a sacrifice, mixed with oil, a fourth of a hin.

relationship: parallel continual morning offering of lamb, grain and oil
rationale: Ezekiel joins the lamb, grain offering and oil in a continual morning burnt offering. Exodus likewise combines a morning lamb with flour and oil in its continual ritual, while additionally prescribing evening offerings and wine libations not named in this Ezekiel unit.
source_text: You all will prepare the lamb, the grain offering, and the oil; you all will prepare them in the morning as a continual burnt offering.

target_units.text: This is what you shall offer on the altar: two year-old lambs without blemish each day continually, a continual offering.
Offer one lamb in the morning and the second in the evening.
With one lamb offer a tenth measure of fine flour mixed with a quarter hin of beaten oil, and a quarter hin of wine as a libation.
Offer the second lamb in the evening, with the same sacrifice and libation as in the morning, as a fragrant aroma, an offering to the Lord,
as a continual sacrifice throughout your generations, at the doors of the Tent of Testimony before the Lord, where I will be made known to you, to speak to you.

relationship: same-chapter distinction between sons' inheritance and servants' temporary gifts
rationale: A gift from the ruler's inheritance to his son becomes an inherited possession. Verse 17 reaffirms the sons' inheritance while limiting a servant's gift to the year of release, explaining the different treatment of these named recipients.
source_text: Thus says the Lord God: If the ruler gives one of his sons a gift from his inheritance, this will belong to his sons as an inherited possession.

target_units.text: If he gives a gift to one of his servants, it will belong to him until the year of release, and he will return it to the ruler. But the inheritance of his sons will belong to them.

relationship: related restoration of possession in the year of release
rationale: A servant's gift lasts until the year of release and then returns to the ruler. Leviticus likewise commands each person to return to his possession in the year of release, but does not state Ezekiel's particular rule for a ruler's gift to a servant.
source_text: If he gives a gift to one of his servants, it will belong to him until the year of release, and he will return it to the ruler. But the inheritance of his sons will belong to them.

target_units.text: And you shall consecrate the fiftieth year, and proclaim release throughout the land unto all who dwell therein; this shall be a year of release, a signal unto you; and each one shall depart unto his possession, and each of you shall depart unto his ancestral homeland.
This is a signal of release: the fiftieth year shall be a year for you. You shall not sow, reap what grows of itself, or gather its consecrated produce.
For it is a signal of release; it shall be holy to you. You shall eat its produce from the fields.
In the year of release, at its signal, each shall return to his possession.

relationship: contrasting prohibition and indictment of inheritance oppression
rationale: The ruler must use his own possession for his sons rather than seize the people's inheritance and scatter them from it. Micah condemns those who covet fields, oppress houses and plunder a man and his inheritance, describing the property oppression that Ezekiel forbids rulers to practice.
source_text: The ruler will certainly not take from the people’s inheritance to oppress them. He will give his sons an inheritance from his own possession, so that none of My people is scattered from his possession.”

target_units.text: They became people planning troubles and working evil on their beds, and at daybreak they carried them out, because they did not raise their hands to God.
They coveted fields and plundered orphans, oppressed houses and plundered a man and his house, a man and his inheritance.

relationship: related northern holy chambers assigned to priests
rationale: The guide brings the viewer to a north-facing recessed chamber of the priests' holy places and shows a separated place. Ezekiel 42 likewise identifies northern and southern holy chambers used by priests for most-holy offerings, without repeating this unit's entrance route.
source_text: He brought me into the entrance behind the gate, into the north-facing recessed chamber of the priests’ holy places. Look—there was a separated place there.

target_units.text: He said to me, “The recessed chambers toward the north and toward the south, facing the intervening spaces, are the chambers of the holy place. There the priests, the sons of Zadok who draw near to the Lord, will eat the most holy things. There they will place the most holy things—the offering, the offerings for sin, and the offerings for ignorance—for the place is holy.

relationship: related precautions against sanctifying people through holy items
rationale: The priests cook and bake the holy offerings in a designated place so that they do not carry them into the outer court and sanctify the people. Ezekiel 44 similarly requires a change of ministering robes before meeting the people, explicitly preventing their sanctification through those robes; neither text is rewritten as defilement.
source_text: He said to me, “This is the place where the priests will boil the offerings for ignorance and for sin, and there bake the entire grain offering, so as not to carry it out into the outer court and sanctify the people.”

target_units.text: When they go out to the outer court, to the people, they will take off the robes in which they minister, place them in the recessed chambers of the holy places, and put on other robes. They will certainly not sanctify the people with their robes.

relationship: same-chapter identification of kitchens and their sacrificial use
rationale: Kitchens are made beneath the recessed chambers surrounding the four courts. The following explanation identifies these as kitchen houses for the house's ministers to boil the people's sacrificial animals, supplying the stated function of the particular structures.
source_text: There were recessed chambers all around them, around the four, with kitchens made underneath the recessed chambers all around.

target_units.text: He said to me, “These are the kitchen houses, where those ministering to the house will boil the people’s sacrificial animals.”

relationship: related house ministries serving the people's sacrifices
rationale: The kitchen houses serve those ministering to the house when they boil the people's sacrificial animals. Ezekiel 44 likewise assigns house ministry and slaughter of the people's offerings to Levites, comparing the service and its beneficiaries while distinguishing boiling from slaughter.
source_text: He said to me, “These are the kitchen houses, where those ministering to the house will boil the people’s sacrificial animals.”

target_units.text: except the Levites, who sprang away from Me when Israel strayed from Me after their reflections; they will receive their injustice—

—and will serve in My holy places as gatekeepers at the house’s gates and as ministers to the house. They will slaughter the burnt offerings and sacrifices for the people, and stand before the people to serve them.

relationship: parallel water issuing from the Lord's house
rationale: Water flows beneath the open court at the house's east-facing front, descending from the right side toward the altar. Joel likewise pictures a spring coming from the Lord's house to water the Wadi of Rushes; it does not give Ezekiel's court or altar details.
source_text: He brought me to the house’s vestibules, and look—water was flowing out beneath the open court toward the east, for the house’s front faced east. The water was descending from the right side, from the south toward the altar.

target_units.text: On that day mountains will drip sweetness, hills will flow with milk, and all Judah’s water outlets will flow with water. A spring will come out of the Lord’s house and water the Wadi of Rushes.

relationship: same-chapter tracing of the waters to the eastern exterior
rationale: After the north-gate exit and circuit to the east-facing court gate, the water is again seen flowing from the right side. Verse 1 had described that right-side flow at the house and altar, connecting the two viewpoints without replacing the supplied open-court wording with a threshold.
source_text: He brought me out by the north gate and led me around outside to the court’s gate facing east. Look—the water was flowing down from the right side.

target_units.text: He brought me to the house’s vestibules, and look—water was flowing out beneath the open court toward the east, for the house’s front faced east. The water was descending from the right side, from the south toward the altar.

relationship: repeated measuring figure with an instrument in his hand
rationale: The man goes out with a measure in his hand, measures a thousand and passes through the water of release. The vision's earlier introduction likewise places a builders' cord and measuring reed in the man's hand; the comparison concerns the measuring figure, not an unstated ankle depth.
source_text: As the man went out opposite, with a measure in his hand, he measured a thousand with the measure and went through the water—water of release.

target_units.text: He brought me in there, and behold, a man whose appearance was like gleaming copper. In his hand were a builders’ cord and a measuring reed, and he stood at the gate.

relationship: same-chapter progression from crossed depths to uncrossable water
rationale: The measuring figure passes through water up to the thighs and then the waist after successive measurements. The next unit describes a further thousand measured and an inability to go through the violently surging water, providing the particular continuation of these crossings.
source_text: He measured a thousand and went through water up to the thighs. He measured a thousand and went through water up to the waist.

target_units.text: He measured a thousand and could not go through, for the water surged violently like the rush of a torrent that they will not cross.

relationship: same-chapter progression from crossed depths to uncrossable water
rationale: After another measurement the water surges too violently to cross. The preceding unit had allowed passage through thigh-deep and waist-deep water, making the changed ability to cross explicit without inserting swimming or an earlier ankle-depth stage.
source_text: He measured a thousand and could not go through, for the water surged violently like the rush of a torrent that they will not cross.

target_units.text: He measured a thousand and went through water up to the thighs. He measured a thousand and went through water up to the waist.

relationship: repeated vision question addressed to the son of man
rationale: The question Have you seen, son of man? repeats the question at the beginning of the guided vision. Ezekiel 40 additionally commands seeing, hearing, attending and showing Israel what is seen, whereas this unit then leads the viewer to the river's edge.
source_text: He said to me, “Have you seen, son of man?” Then he led me to the river’s edge.

target_units.text: The man said to me, ‘Have you seen, son of man? See with your eyes, hear with your ears and set in your heart everything I show you, for you have entered here so that it might be shown to you. You will show Israel’s house everything you see.’

relationship: same-chapter development of the trees on both riverbanks
rationale: Very many trees appear on both sides of the river's edge. Verse 12 returns to those two banks and describes edible trees, unfailing fruit and growth for health, explaining their provision rather than merely repeating the presence of vegetation.
source_text: As I returned, look—very many trees were on the river’s edge, on both sides.

target_units.text: Along the river, on its edge on both sides, every edible tree will grow. Nothing upon it will grow old, nor will its fruit fail. In its newness it will bear its first crop, because these waters flow from the holy places. Their fruit will be for food and their growth for health.

relationship: parallel prophetic healing of waters
rationale: The water flowing into eastern Galilee and descending into Arabia reaches the sea and will heal the waters. In the Elisha episode, the Lord likewise declares the bad waters healed and ends death or loss of offspring from them; the locations and the target's use of salt remain distinct.
source_text: He said to me, “This water flowing out into eastern Galilee was descending into Arabia and coming as far as the sea, to the water of the outlet; it will heal the waters.

target_units.text: The men of the city said to Elisha, ‘Behold, the city’s settlement is good, as the lord sees, but the waters are bad and the land is bereaved of offspring.’
Elisha said, ‘Bring me a new small water jar and put salt in it.’ They brought it to him.
Elisha went out to the outlet of the waters, threw salt there, and said, ‘Thus says the Lord: I have healed these waters. No longer will death or loss of offspring come from there.’
The waters have remained healed to this day, according to the word Elisha spoke.

relationship: related abundance of living creatures in waters
rationale: The river brings life to swarming creatures and an abundance of fish. Genesis likewise brings living creatures forth from the waters and commands them to multiply and fill the seas, comparing aquatic abundance in restoration and creation without making the scenes identical.
source_text: Every life among the swarming living creatures will live wherever the river comes. There will be very many fish there, because this water has arrived there, and it will become healthy and live. Everything over which the river comes will live.

target_units.text: And God said, “Let the waters bring forth living creatures that move, and birds that fly above the earth across the firmament of heaven.” And it was so.

And God made the great sea creatures, and every living creature that moves, which the waters brought forth according to their kinds, and every winged bird according to its kind. And God saw that they were good.
And God blessed them, saying, “Grow and multiply, and fill the waters in the seas; and let the birds multiply upon the earth.”

relationship: contrasting settings for the image of a net-drying place
rationale: The fishers' net-drying place accompanies an exceedingly great multitude of fish in the river vision. Tyre's oracle also names a drying place for nets, but as a smooth rock after destruction with no rebuilding; the shared concrete image serves different restoration and ruin settings.
source_text: Fishers will stand there from Aingadin to Ainagalim; there will be a drying place for nets. It will be by itself, and its fish will be like the fish of the Great Sea, an exceedingly great multitude.

target_units.text: I will make you a smooth rock, a drying place for nets. You will certainly not be rebuilt, for I have spoken, says the Lord.

relationship: same-chapter exception to the waters' healing
rationale: At the outlet, turning and overflow, the source says they will not be healed and are given over to salt. Verses 8–9 had promised healed waters and life wherever the river comes, so this line supplies a stated exception rather than permitting an unqualified claim that every surrounding place is healed.
source_text: At its outlet, at its turning, and at its overflow, they will certainly not be healed; they are given over to salt.

target_units.text: He said to me, “This water flowing out into eastern Galilee was descending into Arabia and coming as far as the sea, to the water of the outlet; it will heal the waters.

Every life among the swarming living creatures will live wherever the river comes. There will be very many fish there, because this water has arrived there, and it will become healthy and live. Everything over which the river comes will live.

relationship: related waterside trees with enduring fruitfulness
rationale: Ezekiel's edible trees stand beside waters from the holy places, with no failing fruit and growth for health. The psalm's figure likewise stands beside water, bears fruit in season and retains its leaf; the source's newness and first-crop wording is not replaced with an unstated monthly schedule.
source_text: Along the river, on its edge on both sides, every edible tree will grow. Nothing upon it will grow old, nor will its fruit fail. In its newness it will bear its first crop, because these waters flow from the holy places. Their fruit will be for food and their growth for health.

target_units.text: He will be like the tree planted beside the outlets of waters, which will give its fruit in its season, and whose leaf will not fall off; and everything he does will be prospered.

relationship: related tribal allocation of the bounded land with different stated scope
rationale: Ezekiel introduces boundaries for an inheritance to twelve tribes and an addition of a measured portion. Numbers likewise assigns the land by lot, there to nine tribes and half Manasseh because two tribes and half Manasseh already received allotments; no Joseph-specific double portion is inserted into Ezekiel's wording.
source_text: Thus says the Lord God: These are the boundaries of the land you will allot as an inheritance to the twelve tribes of the sons of Israel—an addition of a measured portion.

target_units.text: And Moses commanded the sons of Israel, saying: This is the land that you shall inherit by lot, as the Lord prescribed unto Moses to give to the nine tribes and the half-tribe of Manasseh.
For the tribe of the sons of Reuben and the tribe of the sons of Gad according to their ancestral houses, and the half-tribe of Manasseh, have received their allotments.
The two tribes and the half-tribe have received their allotments across the Jordan opposite Jericho, from the south toward the east.

relationship: shared hand-pledged land promise to the fathers
rationale: God identifies the inherited land as that for which He raised His hand to give it to the fathers. Exodus likewise joins God's outstretched hand, the land promised to Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, and its gift as an inheritance, naming the fathers whom this unit leaves collective.
source_text: You will inherit it, each like his brother, the land for which I raised My hand to give it to their fathers. This land will fall to you as an inheritance.

target_units.text: I will bring you into the land concerning which I stretched out My hand to give it to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. I will give it to you as an inheritance. I am the Lord.’”

relationship: shared northern boundary landmarks at the Great Sea and Hamath
rationale: Ezekiel's north boundary begins from the Great Sea and runs toward the entrance of Hamath. Numbers likewise describes a northern boundary from the Great Sea toward Hamath's entrance, while its other supplied place forms are not silently identified with Ezekiel's Seddada.
source_text: These are the boundaries of the land toward the north: from the Great Sea, descending and dividing at the entrance of Hamath—Seddada,

target_units.text: And this shall be your boundary toward the north: from the Great Sea you shall measure out for yourselves beside the mountain, the mountain;
and from the mountain, the mountain, you shall measure out for them toward the entrance into Hamath; and its endpoint shall be the boundaries of Sarada.
And the boundary shall extend to Dephrona, and its endpoint shall be Hazar-enan. This shall be your northern boundary.

relationship: repeated northern boundary landmarks at Damascus and Hamath
rationale: The listed places are situated between the boundaries of Damascus and Hamath. The later northern outline again names Damascus and Hamath as boundary landmarks; this link rests on those explicit names, not on an unverified mapping of Berotha, Sebraim, Heliam or Saunan.
source_text: Berotha, Sebraim, Heliam, between the boundaries of Damascus and the boundaries of Hamath, the court of Saunan, which are above the boundaries of Auranitis.

target_units.text: These are the names of the tribes: from the northern beginning, along the side of the descending, dividing way toward the entrance of Hamath, the court of Ainan, the boundary of Damascus toward the north, along the side of Hamath’s court; the eastern parts as far as the sea will belong to them—Dan, one portion.

relationship: repeated court of Ainan and northern Damascus boundary
rationale: The boundary description includes the court of Ainan, Damascus and the northern parts. The next chapter's northern starting boundary likewise names the court of Ainan and Damascus toward the north, repeating these particular landmarks in the tribal-allocation outline.
source_text: These are the boundaries from the sea, from the court of Ainan, the boundaries of Damascus, and the parts toward the north.

target_units.text: These are the names of the tribes: from the northern beginning, along the side of the descending, dividing way toward the entrance of Hamath, the court of Ainan, the boundary of Damascus toward the north, along the side of Hamath’s court; the eastern parts as far as the sea will belong to them—Dan, one portion.

relationship: shared Jordan boundary on the eastern side
rationale: Ezekiel makes the Jordan a boundary in the eastern parts, ending at the sea east of Palm Grove. Numbers likewise uses the Jordan in its eastern boundary and names the Salt Sea as the endpoint; the differently supplied endpoint descriptions are preserved without requiring their identification.
source_text: The eastern parts lie between Auranitis and Damascus, and between Galaaditis and the land of Israel; the Jordan marks the boundary as far as the sea east of Palm Grove. These are the eastern parts.

target_units.text: And you shall measure out for yourselves the eastern boundary from Hazar-enan unto Shepham.
And the boundary shall descend from Shepham to Arbela, from the east toward the springs. The boundary shall descend to Bela, along the eastern ridge of the Sea of Chennara.
And the boundary shall descend to the Jordan, and its endpoint shall be the Salt Sea. This shall be your land and its surrounding boundaries.

relationship: repeated southwestern boundary through Thaiman and Marimoth Kades
rationale: The south and southwest boundary runs from Thaiman through the water of Marimoth Kades to the Great Sea. The later account repeats those named landmarks as Gad's southwest boundary, while omitting this unit's Palm Grove mention.
source_text: The parts toward the south and southwest run from Thaiman and Palm Grove to the water of Marimoth Kades, extending to the Great Sea. This is the south and southwest side.

target_units.text: From Gad’s boundaries toward the southwest, its boundaries will run from Thaiman and the water of Marimoth Kades, an inheritance as far as the Great Sea.

relationship: shared Great Sea as the sea-facing boundary
rationale: The Great Sea forms the sea-facing boundary, here extending opposite Hamath's entrance. Numbers likewise expressly makes the Great Sea the sea boundary, without repeating the Hamath endpoint in that unit.
source_text: This is the side of the Great Sea: it forms the boundary as far as opposite the entrance of Hamath, as far as its entrance. These are the sea-facing parts of Hamath.

target_units.text: And for your sea boundary, the Great Sea shall mark the limit. This shall be your sea boundary.

relationship: repeated instruction to allot the mapped land among Israel's tribes
rationale: After the boundary description, the land is to be divided for Israel's tribes. The next chapter's conclusion likewise identifies the land to be allotted among those tribes and their divisions, there explicitly using the casting of lots.
source_text: You will divide this land for them, for the tribes of Israel.

target_units.text: This is the land you will cast lots for among Israel’s tribes, and these are their divisions, says the Lord God.

relationship: shared treatment of resident foreigners as native-born
rationale: Sojourners dwelling among Israel who have fathered sons are to be treated as native-born and share an inheritance. Leviticus likewise treats the resident foreigner as the native and forbids oppression, but does not state Ezekiel's qualification about fathering sons or its land-inheritance grant.
source_text: You will cast lots for it for yourselves and for the sojourners dwelling among you who have fathered sons among you. They will be to you as native-born among the sons of Israel; with you they will eat from an inheritance among Israel’s tribes.

target_units.text: If a resident foreigner comes to you in your land, you shall not oppress him.
The resident foreigner who approaches you shall be as the native among you; and you shall love him as yourself, for you were resident foreigners in the land of Egypt; I am the Lord your God.

relationship: same-chapter repeated inheritance grant to sojourners
rationale: The supplied line gives an inheritance in a tribe of sojourners, among the sojourners with them. Verse 22 had granted resident sojourners a share alongside Israel's tribes; the repeated inclusion is retained without replacing this unit's unusual tribal wording with a conventional relocation rule.
source_text: They will be in a tribe of sojourners, among the sojourners who are with them; there you will give them an inheritance, says the Lord God.

target_units.text: You will cast lots for it for yourselves and for the sojourners dwelling among you who have fathered sons among you. They will be to you as native-born among the sons of Israel; with you they will eat from an inheritance among Israel’s tribes.

relationship: related territorial allotment for Dan
rationale: Dan receives the first named northern portion in Ezekiel's east-to-sea arrangement. Joshua likewise assigns Dan a lot, there the seventh, with named towns and a boundary near Joppa; the named tribal inheritance corresponds without making the locations or allocation order identical.
source_text: These are the names of the tribes: from the northern beginning, along the side of the descending, dividing way toward the entrance of Hamath, the court of Ainan, the boundary of Damascus toward the north, along the side of Hamath’s court; the eastern parts as far as the sea will belong to them—Dan, one portion.

target_units.text: The seventh lot came out for Dan.
Their borders were Sarath and Asa, cities of Sammaus,
Salabin, Ammon, and Silatha,
Ailon, Timnah, and Ekron,
Alkatha, Begethon, and Gebeelan,
Azor, Banaibakat, and Gath-rimmon,
From the sea, Jerakon was a boundary near Joppa.
This is the inheritance of the tribe of the sons of Dan according to their divisions—their cities and their villages.

relationship: related territorial allotment for Asher
rationale: Asher's portion extends from Dan's boundaries across the eastern and sea-facing parts. Joshua likewise gives Asher an inheritance, there the fifth lot with a boundary reaching Sidon the Great, preserving a different detailed description of the same tribe's allotment.
source_text: From Dan’s boundaries, from the eastern parts to the sea-facing parts—Asher, one portion.

target_units.text: The fifth lot came out for Asher.
Their borders extended from Eleketh, Aleph, Baithok, and Keaph,
and Elimelech, Amiel, and Maasa; it shall join Carmel toward the sea, and Sion and Labanath.
It shall turn from the sunrise to Bethegeneth and join Zebulun, and from Gai and Phtaiel on the north the boundary shall enter Saphthaibaithme and Inael and pass to Choba Masomel,
and Elbon, Raab, Ememaon, and Kanthan, as far as Sidon the Great.
The boundary shall turn to Ramah and as far as the spring of Masphassat and the Tyrians; the boundary shall turn to Jasiph, and its endpoint shall be the sea, and from Leb and Echozob,
with Archob, Aphek, and Raau.
This is the inheritance of the tribe of the sons of Asher according to their divisions—cities and their villages.

relationship: related Naphtali allotment adjoining Asher
rationale: Naphtali's portion begins at Asher's boundaries in Ezekiel's arrangement. Joshua's Naphtali allotment likewise joins Asher, there toward the sea and with Zebulun to the south; the shared tribal adjacency does not imply identical directional plans.
source_text: From Asher’s boundaries, from the eastern parts to the sea-facing parts—Naphtali, one portion.

target_units.text: The sixth lot came out for Naphtali.
Their borders were Moolam, Mola, Besemiin, Arme, Nabok, and Jephthamai as far as Dodam, and their endpoints were the Jordan.
The boundary shall turn toward the sea to Enath Tabor, pass from there to Jakana, join Zebulun on the south and Asher toward the sea, with the Jordan toward the sunrise.

relationship: related territorial allotment for Manasseh
rationale: Manasseh receives a portion following Naphtali's boundaries. Joshua likewise sets out Manasseh's allotments, identifying Joseph's firstborn and distinguishing Machir's Gilead-and-Bashan inheritance from the other family divisions rather than presenting Ezekiel's east-to-sea strip.
source_text: From Naphtali’s boundaries, from the eastern parts to the sea-facing parts—Manasseh, one portion.

target_units.text: The borders belonged to the tribe of the sons of Manasseh, for he was Joseph’s firstborn: to Machir, Manasseh’s firstborn, the father of Gilead—for he was a man of war—in Gilead and Bashan.

There was also an allotment for the remaining sons of Manasseh according to their divisions: the sons of Jezer, Kelez, Jeziel, Shechem, Symarim, and Hepher. These were the males according to their divisions.

relationship: related Ephraim allotment in relation to Manasseh
rationale: Ephraim's portion extends from Manasseh's boundaries. Joshua likewise describes Ephraim's inheritance and cities set apart for Ephraim amid Manasseh's inheritance, retaining the difference between a boundary adjacency and cities within another tribal allotment.
source_text: From Manasseh’s boundaries, from the eastern parts to the sea-facing parts—Ephraim, one portion.

target_units.text: From Taphou the boundary will go toward the sea to Chelkana, and their endpoint will be at the sea. This is the inheritance of the tribe of Ephraim according to their divisions.
Also there were cities set apart for the sons of Ephraim amid the inheritance of the sons of Manasseh—all the cities and their villages.

relationship: related territorial allotment for Reuben
rationale: Reuben receives an east-to-sea portion from Ephraim's boundaries. Joshua likewise recounts Reuben's inheritance from Moses, naming the Arnon region and Jordan boundary; it supplies a different territorial description rather than the same sequence of neighboring strips.
source_text: From Ephraim’s boundaries, from the eastern parts to the sea-facing parts—Reuben, one portion.

target_units.text: Moses gave an inheritance to the tribe of Reuben according to their divisions.
Their borders were from Aroer facing the Arnon ravine, and the city in the Arnon ravine, and all the Misor,
as far as Heshbon and all the cities in the Misor, Dibon, Bamoth-baal, and the house of Beelmon,
Jahaz, Kedemoth, and Mephaath,
Kiriathaim, Sibmah, Serada, and Sior on Mount Emak,
Beth-peor, Asedoth Phasga, and Beth-jeshimoth,

all the cities of the Misor and all the kingdom of Sihon king of the Amorites, whom Moses struck, together with the leaders of Midian—Evi, Rekem, Zur, Hur, and Reba—rulers under Sihon, and those who lived in the land.
They also killed Balaam son of Beor, the diviner, in the onslaught.
The borders of Reuben were: the Jordan as boundary. This was the inheritance of the sons of Reuben according to their divisions—their cities and their settlements.

relationship: related territorial boundaries for Judah
rationale: Judah receives a portion from Reuben's boundaries. Joshua likewise delineates Judah's territory, beginning from Idumea and the wilderness of Zin on the southwest and ending that boundary at the sea, without reproducing Ezekiel's neighboring-tribe arrangement.
source_text: From Reuben’s boundaries, from the eastern parts to the sea-facing parts—Judah, one portion.

target_units.text: The borders of the tribe of Judah according to their divisions extended from the borders of Idumea, from the wilderness of Zin as far as Kadesh toward the southwest.
Their borders on the southwest extended to the edge of the Salt Sea, from the ridge stretching toward the southwest,
and it passes opposite the ascent of Akrabin, goes around Senna, goes up from the southwest to Kadesh-barnea, goes out to Hezron, ascends to Addara, and goes around the region west of Kadesh.
It goes toward Azmon and will pass through as far as the ravine of Egypt; the boundary will end at the sea. These are their borders on the southwest.

relationship: related sanctuary within a reserved holy land portion
rationale: The first portion adjoining Judah has the holy place in its midst. Ezekiel 45 likewise reserves a measured area containing the sanctuary, there stating a twenty-five-thousand by ten-thousand plot; the counterpart concerns the sanctuary-bearing reservation rather than identical outer dimensions.
source_text: From Judah’s boundaries, from the eastern parts to the sea-facing parts, will be the first portion set apart, twenty-five thousand in breadth, with a length like one of the portions from the eastern parts to the sea-facing parts. The holy place will be in their midst.

target_units.text: From this measured area you will measure a length of twenty-five thousand and a breadth of ten thousand. In it will be the sanctuary, the most holy place.

relationship: related measured first portion set apart for the Lord
rationale: The Lord's first portion is twenty-five thousand long and twenty-five thousand broad. Ezekiel 45 also sets apart a holy first portion with that length but gives a breadth of twenty thousand; the differing stated extents remain visible.
source_text: The first portion they set apart for the Lord will be twenty-five thousand long and twenty-five thousand broad.

target_units.text: “When you measure out the land as an inheritance, you will set apart a first portion for the Lord, a holy part of the land, twenty-five thousand long and twenty thousand broad. It will be holy throughout all its boundaries all around.

relationship: repeated priestly sacred plot and sanctuary provision
rationale: The priests' holy portion measures twenty-five thousand by ten thousand, with the mountain of the holy places in its midst. Ezekiel 45 likewise gives a plot with those dimensions containing the sanctuary and then assigns the land to ministering priests, additionally mentioning their houses.
source_text: From these will be the first portion of the holy areas for the priests: twenty-five thousand toward the north, a breadth of ten thousand toward the sea, a breadth of ten thousand toward the east, and a length of twenty-five thousand toward the south. The mountain of the holy places will be in its midst,

target_units.text: From this measured area you will measure a length of twenty-five thousand and a breadth of ten thousand. In it will be the sanctuary, the most holy place.
It will be land for the priests who minister in the holy place, for those who draw near to minister to the Lord. It will be a place for their houses, set apart for their sanctification.

relationship: repeated fidelity of Zadok's sons during Israel's straying
rationale: The consecrated sons of Zadok kept the house's duties when Israel and the Levites strayed. Ezekiel 44 likewise contrasts the Zadokite priests' fidelity during Israel's straying and grants them approach and service in God's holy places, explaining their distinct priestly standing.
source_text: for the consecrated priests, the sons of Zadok, who keep the duties of the house and did not stray when the sons of Israel strayed, as the Levites strayed.

target_units.text: The Levitical priests, the sons of Zadok, who kept the duties of My holy places when the house of Israel strayed from Me, will approach Me to minister to Me. They will stand before Me to offer sacrifice, fat, and blood to Me, says the Lord God.
They will enter My holy places and approach My table to minister to Me, and they will keep My duties.

relationship: related holy land becoming a priestly possession
rationale: The priests receive a most-holy first portion from the land's first portions, from the Levites' boundaries. Leviticus likewise describes a consecrated field becoming holy to the Lord and the priest's possession after release, but through a different consecration-and-redemption procedure rather than Ezekiel's territorial plan.
source_text: They will have the first portion given from the land’s first portions, most holy, from the Levites’ boundaries.

target_units.text: If he does not redeem the field and sells the field to another man, he shall no longer redeem it.
When the release has passed, the field shall be holy unto the Lord like land set apart. It shall become the priest’s possession.

relationship: repeated Levite allotment dimensions with an additional total
rationale: The Levites' adjoining plot is stated as twenty-five thousand by ten thousand, followed by a whole breadth of twenty thousand. Ezekiel 45 likewise gives the Levites twenty-five thousand by ten thousand with dwelling cities; the later additional breadth clause is not flattened into the earlier measurement.
source_text: The Levites will have the land adjoining the priests’ boundaries, twenty-five thousand long and ten thousand broad. The whole length will be twenty-five thousand and the breadth twenty thousand.

target_units.text: An area twenty-five thousand long and ten thousand broad will belong to the Levites who minister to the house, as their possession, with cities in which to dwell.

relationship: parallel protection of Levitical land from sale
rationale: The land adjoining the priests' allotment may not be sold or measured out, and its first produce may not be removed because it is holy to the Lord. Leviticus likewise protects the fields set apart for Levite cities from sale as their everlasting possession, without repeating Ezekiel's first-produce clause.
source_text: None of it will be sold or measured out, nor will the land’s first produce be taken away, for it is holy to the Lord.

target_units.text: And the cities of the Levites—the houses in their cities of possession—shall always be redeemable by the Levites.

And whosoever redeems from the Levites, the sale of their houses in the city of their possession shall go out at the release; for the houses in the cities of the Levites are their possession among the sons of Israel.
And the fields set apart for their cities shall not be sold, for this is their everlasting possession.

relationship: repeated city allocation of five thousand beside twenty-five thousand
rationale: The remaining five thousand in breadth alongside twenty-five thousand serves the city, dwelling and intervening space. Ezekiel 45 likewise gives the city a possession five thousand broad and twenty-five thousand long for the whole house of Israel, while this unit places the city in its midst.
source_text: The five thousand remaining in breadth alongside the twenty-five thousand will be a forewall for the city, for dwelling and its intervening space. The city will be in its midst.

target_units.text: You will give the city a possession five thousand broad and twenty-five thousand long; like the first portion of the holy areas, these will be for the whole house of Israel.

relationship: same-chapter arithmetic relation between city sides and circuit
rationale: Each of the city's four sides measures four thousand five hundred. Their sum is eighteen thousand, matching the circuit stated in verse 35; this numerical relation supplies no interpretation of the later unit's unusual city-name clause.
source_text: These are its measurements: on the north, four thousand five hundred; on the south, four thousand five hundred; on the east, four thousand five hundred; and toward the sea, four thousand five hundred.

target_units.text: The circuit will be eighteen thousand. And the city’s name, from whatever day it comes into being, will be its name.”

relationship: same-chapter relation of city width and surrounding intervals
rationale: The two hundred fifty intervals on each opposing side, added to the city's four-thousand-five-hundred width, total five thousand. That matches the remaining breadth assigned to the city and intervening space in verse 15, an arithmetic relation within this particular city plan.
source_text: The city will have an intervening space: two hundred fifty toward the north, two hundred fifty toward the south, two hundred fifty toward the east, and two hundred fifty toward the sea.

target_units.text: The five thousand remaining in breadth alongside the twenty-five thousand will be a forewall for the city, for dwelling and its intervening space. The city will be in its midst.

These are its measurements: on the north, four thousand five hundred; on the south, four thousand five hundred; on the east, four thousand five hundred; and toward the sea, four thousand five hundred.

relationship: same-chapter identity of workers supplied by the allocated produce
rationale: The remaining land's produce will be bread for the city's workers. Verse 19 identifies those workers as drawn from all Israel's tribes and says they will work it, linking the specified produce to the people cultivating the allocated land.
source_text: The remaining length adjoining the first portions of the holy areas will be ten thousand toward the east and ten thousand toward the sea; these will be the holy place’s first portions, and its produce will be bread for the city’s workers.

target_units.text: The city’s workers, from all Israel’s tribes, will work it.

relationship: related civic provision involving all Israel's tribes
rationale: The city's workers come from all Israel's tribes and work the assigned land. The earlier city allocation is likewise for the whole house of Israel, connecting the civic provision to Israel broadly without asserting that every Israelite personally works the land.
source_text: The city’s workers, from all Israel’s tribes, will work it.

target_units.text: You will give the city a possession five thousand broad and twenty-five thousand long; like the first portion of the holy areas, these will be for the whole house of Israel.

relationship: same-chapter repeated square extent of the first portion
rationale: The entire first portion is twenty-five thousand by twenty-five thousand and is explicitly described as a square. Verse 9 had stated the same length and breadth for the first portion set apart for the Lord; this unit adds its relation to the city's possession.
source_text: The entire first portion will be twenty-five thousand by twenty-five thousand. You will set apart its holy portion as a square, from the city’s possession.

target_units.text: The first portion they set apart for the Lord will be twenty-five thousand long and twenty-five thousand broad.

relationship: repeated royal portions beside the holy and civic allocations
rationale: The ruler receives the remainder on either side of the holy first portions and the city's possession, toward the east and sea. Ezekiel 45 likewise positions the ruler's land on the two sides of those same allocations, before this later specification of their extent.
source_text: The remainder will belong to the ruler on this side and that side, from the holy first portions and toward the city’s possession, extending twenty-five thousand in length to the eastern boundaries, and toward the sea extending twenty-five thousand to the sea-facing boundaries, adjoining the ruler’s portions. The first portion of the holy areas and the house’s sanctuary will be in its midst.

target_units.text: The ruler will have land on this side and that side of the first portions of the holy areas and the city’s possession, facing the first portions of the holy areas and facing the city’s possession: the parts toward the sea, and from those toward the sea toward the east. Its length will be like one of the portions, from the sea-facing boundaries, with the length extending to the eastern boundaries of the land.

relationship: related royal land adjoining the city and holy allocations
rationale: The unit relates the Levites' and city's possessions to land belonging to the rulers between Judah and Benjamin. Ezekiel 45 likewise assigns the ruler land beside the holy first portions and city, but does not name these two tribal boundaries in that passage.
source_text: From the Levites’ possession and from the city’s possession, it will be in the midst of the rulers; between Judah’s boundaries and Benjamin’s boundaries it will belong to the rulers.

target_units.text: The ruler will have land on this side and that side of the first portions of the holy areas and the city’s possession, facing the first portions of the holy areas and facing the city’s possession: the parts toward the sea, and from those toward the sea toward the east. Its length will be like one of the portions, from the sea-facing boundaries, with the length extending to the eastern boundaries of the land.
It will be his possession in Israel. Israel’s rulers will no longer oppress My people, and the house of Israel will inherit the land according to their tribes.

relationship: related territorial allotment for Benjamin
rationale: Benjamin receives one east-to-sea portion among the remaining tribes. Joshua likewise assigns Benjamin a lot, there placing its borders between Judah and the sons of Joseph; the reference compares the named tribal allotment without identifying the two boundary arrangements.
source_text: As for the remaining tribes, from the eastern parts to the sea-facing parts—Benjamin, one portion.
