target_units.text: The lot of the tribe of Benjamin came out first according to their divisions. The borders of their lot extended between Judah and the sons of Joseph.

relationship: contrasting descriptions of Simeon's allotment
rationale: Simeon receives a portion from Benjamin's boundaries in Ezekiel's sequence. Joshua instead places Simeon's inheritance amid Judah's lot and identifies its towns, preserving the different descriptions of that tribe's territorial placement.
source_text: From Benjamin’s boundaries, from the eastern parts to the sea-facing parts—Simeon, one portion.

target_units.text: The second lot came out for the sons of Simeon, and their inheritance lay amid the lots of the sons of Judah.
Their lot was Beer-sheba, Samaa, and Koladam,
Arsola, Bola, and Asom,
Elthoula, Boula, and Hormah,
Ziklag, Bethmachereb, and Sarsousin,
Batharoth and their fields: thirteen cities, with their villages.
Eremmon, Thalcha, Ether, and Ashan: four cities, with their villages
around their cities as far as Barek, going toward Bameth on the southwest. This is the inheritance of the tribe of the sons of Simeon according to their divisions.
The inheritance of the tribe of the sons of Simeon came from Judah’s lot, because the portion of the sons of Judah was larger than theirs. So the sons of Simeon inherited amid their lot.

relationship: related territorial allotment for Issachar
rationale: Issachar receives a portion from Simeon's boundaries. Joshua likewise gives Issachar an inheritance, there the fourth lot with named towns and a boundary ending at the Jordan; it does not repeat Ezekiel's uniform east-to-sea arrangement.
source_text: From Simeon’s boundaries, from the eastern parts to the sea-facing parts—Issachar, one portion.

target_units.text: The fourth lot came out for Issachar.
Their borders included Jazel, Chasaloth, and Shunem,
Agin, Siona, Reeroth, and Anachereth,
Dabiron, Kison, and Rebes,
Remmas, Jeon, Tomman, Aimarek, and Bersaphes.
The boundary shall join Gaithbor and Salim toward the sea and Bethsamys, and its boundary shall end at the Jordan.
This is the inheritance of the tribe of the sons of Issachar according to their divisions—the cities and their villages.

relationship: related territorial allotment for Zebulun
rationale: Zebulun receives a portion from Issachar's boundaries. Joshua likewise describes Zebulun's inheritance, there the third lot with named borders, cities and villages, rather than Ezekiel's sequence of neighboring tribal portions.
source_text: From Issachar’s boundaries, from the eastern parts to the sea-facing parts—Zebulun, one portion.

target_units.text: The third lot came out for Zebulun according to their divisions. The borders of their inheritance shall be Esedek,
Gola; their borders are the sea and Maragella. It shall join Beth-arabah at the ravine facing Jekman.
It turned back from Seddouk opposite the east, to Bethsamys at the borders of Chaselothaith; it will pass to Daberoth and ascend to Phangai.
From there it will turn opposite the east toward Gebere, toward the city of Katasem, and pass to Remmona, Amathar, Aoza.
The boundary will turn on the north toward Amoth, and their endpoint shall be Gaiphael,
with Katanath, Nabaal, Symoon, Jericho, and Bethman.
This is the inheritance of the tribe of the sons of Zebulun according to their divisions—cities and their villages.

relationship: contrasting descriptions of Gad's landed inheritance
rationale: Gad receives the next portion from Zebulun's boundaries, extending from the eastern to sea-facing parts. Joshua instead recounts Gad's inheritance from Moses with cities of Gilead and a Jordan boundary extending toward the Sea of Chinnereth, preserving the different territorial descriptions.
source_text: From Zebulun’s boundaries, from the eastern parts to the sea-facing parts—Gad, one portion.

target_units.text: Moses gave an inheritance to the sons of Gad according to their divisions.
Their borders were Jazer, all the cities of Gilead, and half the land of the sons of Ammon, as far as Aroer facing Rabbah,
and from Heshbon to Ramoth toward Mizpah, and Betonim and Mahanaim, as far as the borders of Debir;

and in Emek: Beth-haram, Bethanabra, Succoth, and Zaphon, and the rest of the kingdom of Sihon king of Heshbon. The Jordan shall form the boundary as far as a part of the Sea of Chinnereth beyond the Jordan on the east.
This was the inheritance of the sons of Gad according to their divisions—their cities and their settlements.

relationship: repeated southwestern boundary through Thaiman and Marimoth Kades
rationale: Gad's southwest boundary runs from Thaiman and the water of Marimoth Kades to the Great Sea. The preceding land-boundary account uses those same landmarks on its south and southwest side, additionally naming Palm Grove there.
source_text: From Gad’s boundaries toward the southwest, its boundaries will run from Thaiman and the water of Marimoth Kades, an inheritance as far as the Great Sea.

target_units.text: The parts toward the south and southwest run from Thaiman and Palm Grove to the water of Marimoth Kades, extending to the Great Sea. This is the south and southwest side.

relationship: parallel allocation by lots among Israel's tribes
rationale: The closing declaration identifies the land to be allotted among Israel's tribes and their divisions. Numbers likewise commands inheritance by lot according to tribes and ancestral houses, there adding a population-based adjustment that this closing Ezekiel unit does not repeat.
source_text: This is the land you will cast lots for among Israel’s tribes, and these are their divisions, says the Lord God.

target_units.text: And you shall inherit their land by lot according to your tribes. Increase the possession of the larger groups and decrease that of the smaller groups. Wherever his name comes out shall be his. You shall inherit according to the tribes of your ancestral houses.

relationship: related tribal names assigned to city gates and priestly stones
rationale: The city gates bear Israel's tribal names, with Reuben, Judah and Levi named on the north. Exodus likewise assigns the twelve tribal names to the oracle-piece's stones, comparing representation through tribal names rather than equating the objects, positions or engraving methods.
source_text: The city’s gates will bear the names of Israel’s tribes. Three gates will face north: one gate of Reuben, one gate of Judah, and one gate of Levi.

target_units.text: The stones shall bear the names of the sons of Israel, twelve according to their names, each engraved like a seal with the name of one of the twelve tribes.

relationship: same-chapter arithmetic relation between circuit and four city sides
rationale: The stated circuit of eighteen thousand equals the four sides of four thousand five hundred given in verse 16. This supports the measured-city connection only: the supplied city-name clause is preserved and is not replaced by the traditional name The Lord is there.
source_text: The circuit will be eighteen thousand. And the city’s name, from whatever day it comes into being, will be its name.”

target_units.text: These are its measurements: on the north, four thousand five hundred; on the south, four thousand five hundred; on the east, four thousand five hundred; and toward the sea, four thousand five hundred.
